thesis: Oracle has transformed from a mature database licensing company into one of the fastest-growing hyperscale cloud providers, with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) capacity now the binding constraint on revenue rather than demand. A record remaining performance obligation (RPO) backlog exceeding $450B — driven by multi-year AI training and inference contracts including Stargate-related capacity — provides multi-year revenue visibility that is unmatched in enterprise software. The core question is execution: whether Oracle can build data-center capacity fast enough, fund the capex, and convert backlog into margin-accretive revenue. At ~$142 the stock offers a positive risk/reward for investors who believe OCI backlog conversion is durable, tempered by heavy capex compressing near-term free cash flow.

drivers: OCI revenue sustains 50%+ growth as record RPO backlog above $450B converts on schedule and capacity constraints ease
AI training and inference demand (OpenAI/Stargate-class contracts, multicloud database deals with AWS, Azure and Google) keeps the backlog compounding faster than it is recognized
Total revenue reaches a $100B+ run rate by FY2028 with cloud crossing 50% of the mix, driving operating-margin expansion
Free cash flow inflects sharply higher as capex intensity normalizes and high-margin cloud consumption scales

risks: Data-center capex balloons past $40B annually, keeping free cash flow depressed and forcing incremental debt issuance
RPO backlog conversion slips as power, GPU supply, and construction bottlenecks delay capacity coming online
Customer concentration in a handful of mega AI contracts creates renewal and counterparty risk if AI capex cools
Hyperscaler price competition (AWS, Azure, Google) compresses OCI margins before scale benefits are realized

base_case.assumptions: OCI grows 40-50% and total revenue compounds mid-teens to high-teens through FY2028, RPO backlog converts steadily but with some timing slippage, capex remains elevated (~$35B/yr) keeping FCF muted near term, and the market assigns a premium cloud-growth multiple that partially normalizes as free cash flow recovers.

catalysts.event: FY2027 Q1 earnings — first read on RPO backlog trajectory, OCI revenue growth, and capex guidance
Oracle CloudWorld — OCI capacity roadmap, new AI/multicloud database partnerships, and product announcements
FY2027 Q2 earnings — cloud revenue mix, data-center bring-up cadence, and free cash flow trend
FY2027 Q3 earnings — backlog conversion progress and updated FY2027 cloud growth outlook
OCI data-center capacity build-out and Stargate-related capacity coming online, converting RPO into recognized revenue

key_risks: Execution risk on data-center build-out: power availability, GPU supply, and construction timelines could delay backlog conversion
Heavy capex (~$35B+/yr) compresses free cash flow and may require additional debt, raising balance-sheet leverage
Customer concentration in a small number of very large AI contracts creates counterparty and renewal risk
Intense hyperscaler competition from AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud could pressure OCI pricing and margins
A broad slowdown in AI infrastructure spending would undermine the growth premium embedded in the valuation
